title: How a Hurricane Turns Warm Ocean Into a Storm

Sources: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/hurricane.html and National Aeronautics and Space Administration https://spaceplace.nasa.gov/hurricanes/en/ #Science #ScienceFacts #QuantaTale
narration: What turns warm ocean water into a giant spinning storm? A hurricane works like an engine that runs on warm, moist air. As the warm air rises, it leaves an area of lower pressure below. Rising air cools, and its water vapour forms clouds. North of the equator they spin anticlockwise; south of it, clockwise. At the centre an eye forms, calm and clear. Once its sustained winds are strong enough, the storm counts as a hurricane. On land they usually weaken, because the warm ocean no longer feeds them.
